A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

type I 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydroganese in the kidney is localized only in the renal cortex and is present only in the proxymal tubule cells, and the rate-limiting step in the inactivation of prostaglandin is the substrate concentration rather than the coenzyme concentration.
type I 15-hydroxyl-prostaglandin dehy-drogenase is a key enzyme for the inactivation of prostaglandin E2 and prostaglandin F2α and is localized in the proximal tubules of rat kidney.
the type I 15-PGDH is the most important enzyme for the inactivation of prostaglandin in the kidney and the activity of the enzyme is developmentally regulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzyme is localized in the proximal tubule of 3 week old rat kidney and is not in the inner medullary collecting duct as previously reported.
the enzyme may play a role in inactivating prostaglandins produced in the medulla and reaching the proximal tubule.
15-PGDH plays a role in the regulation of PGE2 in the kidney, and that this enzyme may be a target for future therapeutic intervention.
